availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #377. The API states no publication time and keeps no vintages (it serves the current table), so the instant is Treasury's published schedule, not a measured one, and it is NOT VERIFIED from this environment: fiscaldata.treasury.gov (the dataset page that states the schedule) is refused by the proxy, and only the api. host is reachable. The schedule used is that the Daily Treasury Statement for a business day is published at 4:00 PM ET on the next business day. 16:30 ET is declared, 30 minutes after it and the same margin the bill-rate declaration takes over its bulk file's time, so a decision at 16:00 ET on that next business day does not read it and the first decision that does is the one after. The series' meaning and units were checked against FRED's WTREGEN (the H.4.1's weekly average of the TGA): the 7-calendar-day average of the daily closing balances ending each Wednesday, carried across weekends and holidays, matches WTREGEN to within 0.0009 USD billions on every one of the 451 Wednesdays 2018-01-17 to 2026-09-02 (tests/fixtures/snapshots/dts_inputs against funding_inputs/fred-macro-latest-vintage), which also settles that the line named 'Federal Reserve Account', 'Treasury General Account (TGA)' and 'Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance' are one series across the renames. Units: the statement reports USD millions; the adapter divides by 1000.
availability_provenance.publication: Daily Treasury Statement (Bureau of the Fiscal Service), Table I, Operating Cash Balance, served as Fiscal Data's accounting/dts/operating_cash_balance table; published at 4:00 PM ET on the business day after the date it describes.

coverage: Treasury General Account closing balance, daily, 2018-01-02 onwards in the tracked snapshots (the table runs from 2005-10-03)
treasury_dts_tga.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#377), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes (docs/decisions/final-test-preregistration.md, amendment of 7 October 2026): the TGA the published declarations read is FRED's weekly WTREGEN (fred_macro_latest_vintage), and this daily series is read only by the measurement fields tga_daily, tga_daily_change and tga_change_x_reserves (repo_model.measurement_fields). The closing-balance line has had three names (the Federal Reserve Account, the Treasury General Account (TGA), and from the April 2022 redesign the Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance, whose value sits in the open_today_bal column); the adapter reads each in its own column and refuses a date with two closing balances. Each snapshot is one unmodified, year-wide response; a re-fetch can differ.
treasury_dts_tga.provider: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #426. The columns are computed per panel row by repo_model.net_settlement from Fiscal Data's auctions_query records (tests/fixtures/snapshots/net_settlement_inputs/treasury_auctions, fetched 2026-10-08 with ingest.fetch_treasury_auctions), each auction counted from its announcemt_date. The dataset states no announcement clock time. Treasury's usual announcement time, 11:00 a.m. ET, is from general knowledge and was NOT verified from this environment; 12:00 ET is declared, an hour later, so a 16:00 ET decision of the announcement day reads the announcement and no decision before it does. The earliest closing of any auction in the snapshot is 10:00 a.m. (cash management bills announced and held on one day).
availability_provenance.publication: U.S. Treasury auction announcements (offering amount, and the estimate of the publicly held securities maturing on the settlement date), announced days before the auction and the settlement.

coverage: offering amounts and the publicly held maturing estimate of every Treasury auction settling 2018-01-02 to 2026-01-15 in the tracked snapshot
treasury_auction_net_settlement.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#426), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes (docs/decisions/final-test-preregistration.md): the published treasury_auctions source is dated from the settlement and its scheduled availability. These columns are read only by a track that switches them on (repo_model.net_settlement.COLUMN_FIELDS). The maturing figure is the announced estimate of the publicly held maturing amount by security type; a group of auctions announced with no figure (mostly cash management bills) reads zero maturing, so its net is its offering. availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445, from the tracked snapshots of the Desk's operation results (tests/fixtures/snapshots/on_rrp_inputs/nyfed_on_rrp, the same records nyfed_on_rrp reads). The Desk states no publication clock time (nyfed_on_rrp.availability_provenance). The evidence is each record's lastUpdated, the time the Desk last wrote it: a record whose lastUpdated is on its own operation date is public no later than that time, because it cannot be written later than it was first written. Over the 1997 operation dates 2018-01-02 to 2025-12-31 that carry a reverse-repo operation, 1985 have every record last written on the operation date at or before 15:00 New York time (earliest 13:15:20, median 13:15:52, 99th percentile 13:22:17, latest 14:43:00 on 2023-07-17, an operation delayed to close at 14:00). The other 12 are not provable and are excluded, so the column is empty on them: 10 were written again on a later date (2018-03-29, 2018-12-04, 2019-04-18, 2020-04-09, 2020-07-02, 2021-04-01, 2021-09-03, 2021-09-10, 2022-11-17, 2023-01-05), where lastUpdated says nothing about the first write, and 2 were last written on their own date after 15:00 (2018-02-16 at 16:43:22, a record annotated that $14.050 billion less settled than was accepted, and the 2024-10-16 small-value exercise at 16:50:30) and are excluded because the time of their first write is not known. The reading assumes the Desk's API serves a record from the time it is written, which is not stated anywhere and cannot be verified from outside; a record could be written to the Desk's database before the API shows it. 15:00 is declared, 17 minutes after the latest included lastUpdated and an hour before the 16:00 decision. Note the exclusion looks at a record's later rewrites, which no forecast at the time could know; it only removes days, and whether a record was rewritten years later is unrelated to the spread.
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed reverse repo operation results: the operation closes at 13:15 ET and the Desk's API carries the summary of results, last written at lastUpdated; 15:00 ET on the operation date is the declared availability instant for a day whose records were all last written on that date at or before 15:00.

coverage: overnight reverse repo amounts accepted on the operation date, for the dates whose evidence is proven

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445. EXCLUDED: no publication time before 16:00 New York time can be established. Treasury's Daily Treasury Bill Rates page (tests/fixtures/snapshots/treasury_bill_rates_page, fetched 2026-10-09T03:02:41Z, sha256 949a9940...) states that the par yields are derived from indicative bid-side quotations 'obtained by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York at or near 3:30 PM each trading day' and states no time at which the rates are posted. The tracked yearly exports carry a retrieval time only (one fetch, 2026-09-14, or the commit time of the file) and the page keeps no vintages, so no archived copy dates a first posting; the page fetched here already carried the 8 October row when read, some 8 hours after the close. The Federal Reserve's H.15 file, which republishes the rates, is at 16:30 ET (treasury_bill_rates.availability_provenance). Quotes are struck at about 15:30, so a posting before 16:00 would leave under 30 minutes and nothing shows it happened. The input is therefore declared at the end of its own day, which no decision at 16:00 on the same day reads; it enters no nowcast and no forecast of this track.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445. spread_nowcast_bps on the row of day r is computed by repo_model.nowcast from the spread of day r - 1 (SOFR is published at about 08:00 ET on r and declared public at 15:00 ET on r, nyfed_sofr.release_lag) and earlier days, the same-day reverse repo of r (nyfed_on_rrp_sameday, 15:00 on r), the gross Treasury settlement of r (treasury_auctions.scheduled_availability, 15:00 on the panel day before r) and the calendar. Its latest input is therefore public at 15:00 ET on r. Its ridge is fitted on pairs whose target row is at most r - 1. tests/test_nowcast.py checks both by changing every input from row r on, and every label from row r on, and asking the nowcast to stay the same.
availability_provenance.publication: Computed by this repository from the public inputs above; nothing is published.

coverage: a nowcast of the spread (SOFR - IORB, bp) of each panel day, made at 16:00 ET on that day
spread_nowcast.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#445). Read only by a track that switches the column on (repo_model.nowcast.COLUMN_FIELDS). It is the naive nowcast (the spread of day r - 1) wherever the model is not fitted or an input is missing. The constituents' timing is declared here, not through contract.FEATURE_FIELDS, because the as-of rule reads a derived feature at the latest row where every constituent is observable, which would put SOFR's lag on a value that is built for a day before SOFR is public.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #425. The same operation-results endpoint as nyfed_srf and nyfed_on_rrp (markets.newyorkfed.org/api/rp/results/search.json), saved here a calendar year at a time for 2018-01-01 to 2025-12-31 and read for every repo operation, not only the facility's overnight ones. The Desk states no clock time at which results are published; the one timestamp in each record is lastUpdated, a write time. The adapter records it per operation date (the latest lastUpdated of the date's kept operations, New York time) and reads a date's values at the later of that and the declaration below, so a rewritten record can only make a value later. On the snapshots, lastUpdated is on the operation date for all but 2023-05-11 (09:29 the next day, before the declaration), and is later than the declaration for two dates, 2021-09-03 and 2021-09-10, both rewritten on 2021-09-16. The declaration is #45's and #127's conservative reading for the same endpoint: 16:00 ET on the next business day.
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed repo operation results: the temporary open market operations of 2019 and 2020 and the Standing Repo Facility from 2021-07-29. Operations close between 08:30 and 13:45 ET and the Desk publishes a summary of results after each, at no stated clock time. 16:00 ET on the next business day is the conservative availability instant declared here.

coverage: Repo operations (overnight and term) amounts accepted and submitted, the amount-weighted rate accepted and the number of operations that accepted anything, per operation date, 2018-05-09 to 2025-12-31 in the tracked snapshots
nyfed_repo_ops.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#425), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes. repo_accepted and repo_submitted are totalAmtAccepted and totalAmtSubmitted summed over every operation of an operationDate whose operationType is 'Repo' (overnight or term), in USD billions (the API serves US dollars). repo_rate is the accepted-amount-weighted mean of the securities' percentWeightedAverageRate, in percent, and is absent on a date where nothing was accepted at a stated rate. repo_ops_accepting counts the date's operations that accepted anything. A date with no operation has no row; the measurement columns (repo_liquidity) read it as zero. Operations the Desk names small-value exercises in the note are left out. The Desk's operational tests of 2018 and 2019 (about 65 million dollars each, announced by operating-policy notices and not named so in the note) are kept: they are non-zero days. Each yearly snapshot is one unmodified search response; the year in progress changes when re-fetched.
nyfed_repo_ops.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

release_lag.note: Declared 8 October 2026 (#425), as nyfed_srf declares it (#127): a date's results are available at 16:00 ET on the next business day, not at the close, because the Desk states no publication time and lastUpdated is a write time that was rewritten days later on 2021-09-03 and 2021-09-10.

nyfed_repo_ops.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the New York Fed operation-results schema; the empty declaration is not a finding. A date with no row is read as zero take-up by repo_liquidity, a measurement choice declared there.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #442. A sensitivity test of nyfed_repo_ops, not a replacement: the same endpoint, the same yearly snapshots (nyfed_repo_ops/), read at a less conservative instant. Operations close at 13:45 ET (and 08:30 ET from 26 June 2025). The Desk states no clock time at which results are published; the one timestamp, lastUpdated, is a write time. On the facility's 1,617 overnight operations (2021-07-29 to 2026-09-30) it falls a median 0.7 minutes after the close and 3.3 minutes at the 99th percentile (nyfed_srf.availability_provenance, #127). On the tracked snapshots (2018-05-09 to 2025-12-31) only five operation dates were written after 16:00 ET on their own date: 2021-12-28 at 16:10 and 2023-03-22 at 17:22 the same day, 2023-05-11 at 09:29 on the next day, and 2021-09-03 and 2021-09-10, both rewritten on 2021-09-16. A date is therefore read as public at 16:00 ET on its own date, and a date written later is read at the next decision instant at or after its write time (ingest.repo_operation_same_day_available_at); the two rewritten dates stay on the conservative reading because a rewrite cannot establish a first publication. The panel columns (fed_liquidity, suffix _sameday) read a withheld date as zero, as a date with no operation. The published nyfed_srf declaration (16:00 ET on the next business day) is not changed by this source; changing it is Eleonora's decision.
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed repo operation results: the temporary open market operations of 2019 and 2020 and the Standing Repo Facility from 2021-07-29. Operations close between 08:30 and 13:45 ET and the Desk publishes a summary of results after each, at no stated clock time. 16:00 ET on the operation date is the less conservative availability instant tested here.

coverage: Repo operations (overnight and term) amounts accepted and submitted, the amount-weighted rate accepted and the number of operations that accepted anything, per operation date, 2018-05-09 to 2025-12-31 in the tracked snapshots
nyfed_repo_ops_sameday.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#442), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes. A second reading of nyfed_repo_ops: its fields, units and snapshots are those of nyfed_repo_ops (see its limitation); only the availability instant differs, and the dates written after their own 16:00 are withheld by the column assembly, not by this lag (fed_liquidity.assemble, reading same_day).
nyfed_repo_ops_sameday.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

release_lag.note: Declared 9 October 2026 (#442) as a sensitivity test: a date's results are available at 16:00 ET on the operation date itself, because lastUpdated falls a median 0.7 minutes after the close. Unlike the lag, the column assembly withholds the five dates written after 16:00 (ingest.repo_operation_same_day_available_at). The conservative declaration, nyfed_repo_ops.release_lag, is unchanged.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 11 October 2026 for #545. Not a fetched series: the columns are computed per panel row by repo_model.projected_reserves. net_settlement_ahead_{k}d is the announced net Treasury settlement of the next k business days, each auction counted from its announcemt_date as at the declared instant of treasury_auction_net_settlement (12:00 ET on the row's own day). proj_reserves_h{h}, proj_dist_h{h} and proj_change_h{h} roll the reserve level that the as-of rule reads at the row's 16:00 decision forward to the scored day through the flows public by then; every read goes through asof.InformationRule with the scored row one after the decision row, and repo_model.projected_reserves.check_no_future rebuilds a row from the panel cut at it and refuses a column that differs. A row's value is therefore public at 16:00 on its own date.
availability_provenance.publication: metadata/projected_reserves.json declares the rule; its inputs are the registry's reserve_balances (H.4.1 WRESBAL), tga_daily (Daily Treasury Statement), on_rrp, bank_total_assets (H.8) and treasury_auction_net_settlement, each under its own lag.

coverage: one value per panel day to 2025-12-31, from the first day on which the as-of rule reads every input
projected_reserves_columns.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#545), declared here and not in metadata/sources.json for the reason treasury_auction_net_settlement gives. Read only by a track that switches the columns on (repo_model.projected_reserves.COLUMN_FIELDS). The projection rolls the weekly reserve level forward by the Fed liability identity (Treasury account and facility gain what reserves lose); it ignores currency and the Federal Reserve's own asset changes, and it adds no separate runoff leg: the Treasury leg is inside the announced net settlement, and agency MBS paydowns are in no tracked series. No announced TGA path is tracked, so persistence applies beyond the settlements and the expected tax receipts.
projected_reserves_columns.provider: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service

release_lag.note: Declared 11 October 2026 (#545). The value on the row of day t uses only reads the as-of rule allows at 16:00 ET on t (availability_provenance), so the 16:00 ET decision of t reads it.

projected_reserves_columns.reviewed_note: Derived columns: no structural zeros. A hole is a missing input or a row where the rule has no read.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 11 October 2026 for #587. Not a fetched series: the column is computed per panel row by repo_model.satiation. satiation_roll is the declared low quantile of the reserves-to-assets ratios that the as-of rule reads at each of the last 504 panel rows' own 16:00 decisions, up to and including the row's own; each leg of the ratio (reserve_balances, H.4.1; bank_total_assets, H.8) is read at its own latest public row through asof.InformationRule with the scored row one after the decision row, and repo_model.satiation.check_no_future rebuilds a row from the panel cut at it and refuses a level that differs. A row's value is therefore public at 16:00 on its own date.
availability_provenance.publication: metadata/satiation_587.json declares the rule; its inputs are the registry's reserve_balances (H.4.1 WRESBAL) and bank_total_assets (H.8), each under its own lag.

coverage: one value per panel day to 2025-12-31, from the first day on which the as-of rule reads both legs of the ratio
satiation_columns.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#587), declared here and not in metadata/sources.json for the reason projected_reserves_columns gives. Read only by a track that switches the column on (repo_model.satiation.COLUMN_FIELDS). The published scarcity indicator and its 0.12 band are unchanged. The level is a low quantile of a step series (the ratio changes only when a weekly release lands), so each week's ratio counts for as many panel rows as it is the latest public one.
satiation_columns.provider: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.4.1, H.8), as read through the registry

release_lag.note: Declared 11 October 2026 (#587). The value on the row of day t uses only reads the as-of rule allows at 16:00 ET on t (availability_provenance), so the 16:00 ET decision of t reads it.

satiation_columns.reviewed_note: Derived column: no structural zeros. A hole is a row where the rule has no read of a leg.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 12 October 2026 for #598. Not a fetched series: the columns are computed per panel row by repo_model.satiation.build_distance_columns. satiation_dist_roll is the reserves-to-assets ratio that the as-of rule reads at the row's own 16:00 decision minus satiation_roll's level at that row (the rolling level of #587, constants unchanged); satiation_hinge_roll is the percentage points by which that ratio is below the level, 0 at or above it. Each leg of the ratio (reserve_balances, H.4.1 WRESBAL; bank_total_assets, H.8) is read at its own latest public row through asof.InformationRule with the scored row one after the decision row, and repo_model.satiation.check_distance_no_future rebuilds a row from the panel cut at it and refuses a value that differs. A row's value is therefore public at 16:00 on its own date.
availability_provenance.publication: metadata/satiation_distance_598.json declares the rule; its inputs are the registry's reserve_balances (H.4.1 WRESBAL) and bank_total_assets (H.8), each under its own lag, and the rolling level of metadata/satiation_587.json.

coverage: one value per panel day to 2025-12-31, from the first day on which the as-of rule reads both legs of the ratio
satiation_distance_columns.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#598), declared here and not in metadata/sources.json for the reason satiation_columns gives. Read only by a track that switches the columns on (repo_model.satiation.DISTANCE_COLUMN_FIELDS). The published scarcity indicator and its 0.12 band are unchanged. The ratio is a step series (it changes only when a weekly release lands), so a value repeats until the next release moves the ratio or the level.
satiation_distance_columns.provider: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.4.1, H.8), as read through the registry
